title: occupancy-aware-batch-trimmer-with-client-weighted-fairness
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: During multi-region surges we observe bursty occupancy at GPU serving shards that causes p95/p99 latency and token budget SLO violations for high-priority tenants. Current shedding policies are coarse-grained (global token caps, simple token-bucket per-tenant) and either over-provision or unfairly penalize small but latency-sensitive customers.

Proposal: Implement an occupancy-aware batch trimming admission controller that trims batches (number of tokens / requests admitted to a GPU batch) dynamically per-shard based on current queue occupancy and per-tenant fairness weights. The controller applies staged graceful degradation modes: 1) early token-trim (truncate generation inputs or forced-stop), 2) output compression (map verbose outputs to compressed summaries), and 3) synthetic placeholder response with async backfill for low-priority requests. Trim decisions are budgeted by a rolling SLO credit ledger per-tenant and per-service-class to avoid starvation.

Core components: admission-controller hook (in runtime admission path), shard occupancy sampler, batch-trim policy engine (rule- + ML-scored), per-tenant fairness ledger, degradation mode executor (transformer pipeline hooks), and a simulation harness for offline validation. The runtime will expose metrics to Console: admitted_rate, trimmed_tokens, trimmed_requests, fairness_score, per-tenant-slo-credit, and mode_breakdown.
acceptance_criteria: Admission controller can trim batches on a live shard without introducing >2ms p50 overhead in admission path
Under simulated 3x baseline QPS surge, p95 latency for SLA class A decreases by >=18% vs baseline and token cost per effective response reduces >=22%
Per-tenant fairness score distribution shows no tenant with >30% disproportionate trimming for tenants with weight >=0.5
All degradation modes are reversible and have explicit canary flags in Console
Unit + integration tests for admission controller and degradation executor in CI with >=90% branch coverage for policy code paths
Runbook updated and operator-facing toggles implemented for emergency disable/rollback

design_notes:
We chose occupancy-aware trimming instead of strict request rejection to preserve soft-failure semantics for user-facing applications. Fairness ledger uses exponentially-weighted moving average of trimmed-time to smooth transient spikes. ML scoring prototype uses a light-weight gradient-boosted model trained on offline logs to predict cost-sensitivity of trimming (expected degrade in perceived quality). For predictability, policy rules have precedence over ML score at high criticality levels.

Trade-offs: trimming can change output semantics and can increase downstream client complexity. We mitigate by offering structured warnings in responses and an async backfill path for non-critical requests. There is also increased runtime telemetry and bookkeeping cost; we budgeted 2-3% CPU on inference sidecars and use sampling to reduce overhead.
simulation_summary: Initial sims (synthetic tenant mix of 2000 tenants, 12% SLA-A, 28% SLA-B, rest best-effort) with region-local surges showed: trimmed_tokens rose to 18% of total tokens in peak windows, p99 latency reduced from 620ms to 490ms on trimmed shards, and effective successful responses increased 11% due to fewer timeouts. Fairness weighting reduced high-tail trimming for top-ten customers by 64% vs naive trimming. We observed small increases in end-to-end client error explanations for top-quality-sensitive tasks; will add tailored training data for ML scorer. Full sim results and dashboards linked below.
rollout_plan: Stage 1: internal canary in dev region (1 shard) with telemetry sampling and explicit kill switch. Stage 2: limited production canary for low-risk tenants (5% traffic) for 48h. Stage 3: region ramp to 25% then 60% with automated health gates (no SLO regression for SLA-A; trimmed_tokens <= 25%). Stage 4: global enable for all non-enterprise tenants and opt-in enterprise pilots. Each stage duration minimum 48 hours and requires runbook signoff.
monitoring_playbook: Primary alerts: trimmed_tokens_rate > configured threshold, fairness_score drift > 0.2, admitted_rate drop > 10% vs baseline, per-shard admission-hook errors. Dashboards: per-region admitted_rate, per-tenant-slo-credit, mode_breakdown. SLOs to watch: p95 latency by SLA class, token-cost-per-successful-response, error-rate for placeholder responses. Automated rollback triggers on sustained p95 regressions for SLA-A (>5% relative) or critical errors in degradation executor.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: semantic degradation of outputs affects user trust. Mitigation: limit early-token-trim to predictable cutpoints (e.g., max tokens for summarization tasks), expose degradation metadata to clients, and provide async backfill. Risk: bookkeeping overhead leads to performance regressions. Mitigation: aggressive sampling, offload ledger aggregation to sidecar, incremental rollout. Risk: fairness gamification by tenants. Mitigation: tie weights to contractual entitlements and monitor anomalies.
